skill.name: copilot-coding-agent
skill.description: Automates GitHub Copilot Coding Agent assignment from GitHub issues using labels, GitHub Actions, and GraphQL-based setup guidance.
skill.summary: Turn reviewed GitHub issues into Copilot draft pull requests through label-based repository automation.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: Most static findings were markdown backticks, code fences, or documentation links rather than hidden execution or runtime network access. The real concerns are privileged GitHub automation: repo-scoped token handling, local shell scripts, workflow deployment, and bulk labeling that can trigger Copilot draft pull requests. Publish with clear warnings about token scope, script review, and human approval controls.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer a fine-grained token or GitHub App token limited to the target repository and required permissions. Store it only as a secret, avoid printing it, and rotate it regularly.
Include the referenced scripts or link to reviewed source, explain every repository change, and require users to inspect scripts before execution.

remediation.issue: Bulk issue labeling can trigger automated work
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run step, limit bulk operations to reviewed low-risk issues, and require maintainers to approve the resulting draft pull requests and CI runs.

remediation.issue: Command examples are easy to run without context
remediation.suggestion: Mark command snippets as manual operations and document prerequisites, expected effects, and rollback steps beside each command.

semantic_findings.title: Repo-Scoped Token Used for Automation
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires a Personal Access Token with repo scope, registers COPILOT_ASSIGN_TOKEN as a secret, and exports the token before running an assignment script. This is privileged credential handling and could affect repository contents if misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly require a repo-scoped PAT, register it as a repository secret, and export it for a shell script. The risk is credential exposure or overbroad repository access, not hidden exfiltration.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Labels Trigger Code-Producing Pull Requests
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to add the ai-copilot label so GitHub Actions assigns Copilot, which creates branches and draft pull requests. Bulk labeling can start multiple automated code changes without per-issue review if used carelessly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines describe the label-triggered workflow and include a bulk-label command. This is a clear business-logic risk for automated repository changes, although the workflow still produces draft pull requests.

content.value_statement: Teams need a controlled way to delegate reviewed GitHub issues to Copilot Coding Agent. This skill documents a label-based workflow that assigns Copilot, starts implementation, and tracks draft pull requests.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to trigger Copilot Coding Agent by applying an ai-copilot label to GitHub issues.
Documents setup steps for a GitHub Actions workflow that assigns issues to Copilot.
Shows gh CLI examples for creating issues, adding labels, and checking Copilot pull requests.
Describes required GitHub Copilot plans, repository settings, and manual approval limits.
Provides quick-reference commands for setup, assignment, and verification tasks.
limitations: Requires GitHub Copilot Coding Agent access and an enabled repository setting.
Requires authenticated GitHub CLI access and a privileged token for assignment automation.
Does not include the referenced setup or assignment shell scripts in the skill package.
Copilot-created pull requests still need human review, CI approval, and repository permission controls.

use_cases.description: Use reviewed GitHub issues as a queue for Copilot-generated draft pull requests.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation Tickets
use_cases.description: Create clear issues that can be labeled for Copilot after scope and acceptance criteria are approved.

use_cases.title: Maintain Repository Automation
use_cases.description: Set up labels, workflow triggers, secrets, and CI checks for controlled Copilot assignment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Copilot-Ready Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me draft a GitHub issue that is specific enough for Copilot Coding Agent. Include scope, acceptance criteria, files to inspect, and test expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this GitHub issue and tell me whether it is ready for the ai-copilot label. List missing requirements and risks before assignment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Repository Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through setting up label-based Copilot assignment for this repository. Include required permissions, secrets, workflow approval steps, and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Controlled Copilot Queue
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe process for bulk delegating low-risk backlog issues to Copilot. Include triage rules, dry-run checks, CI gates, and human review requirements.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether an issue is ready for Copilot assignment.
output: Readiness status with missing context called out.
Suggested acceptance criteria and test expectations.
A recommendation to label only after review is complete.

output_examples.input: A maintainer wants to set up repository automation.
output: A checklist for Copilot access, GitHub CLI authentication, token scope, and workflow approval.
A reminder to inspect setup scripts before running them.
Verification steps for draft pull requests and CI checks.

output_examples.input: A team wants to process a small technical debt queue.
output: A triage plan that selects simple, well-scoped issues first.
A dry-run review step before labels are applied.
A monitoring plan for draft pull requests, reviewers, and failed checks.

best_practices: Review each issue for scope, acceptance criteria, and test guidance before applying the ai-copilot label.
Use the least privileged token available and rotate it after setup or incident response work.
Require human review, CI approval, and rollback planning for every Copilot-created pull request.
anti_patterns: Do not label vague or high-risk issues before a maintainer reviews the implementation scope.
Do not run setup or assignment scripts before inspecting their contents and expected repository changes.
Do not bulk-label issues without a dry run, rate limits, and a plan for monitoring draft pull requests.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It documents a GitHub issue workflow where an ai-copilot label assigns Copilot Coding Agent and starts a draft pull request.

faq.question: Does it write application code directly?
faq.answer: No. It guides repository automation that asks GitHub Copilot Coding Agent to create code changes in draft pull requests.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: You need GitHub Copilot Coding Agent access, repository settings enabled, GitHub CLI authentication, and appropriate repository permissions.

faq.question: Is a personal access token required?
faq.answer: The skill describes a repo-scoped token for assignment automation. Use the narrowest supported token and protect it as a secret.

faq.question: Can this be used with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as operational guidance for GitHub workflows.

faq.question: What should reviewers check after Copilot opens a draft PR?
faq.answer: Review code quality, security impact, tests, permissions, CI results, and whether the change matches the original issue.
